ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The graph of the function f in the figure consists of two semicircles. The first segment goes from x=-1 to x=1, is located above the x-axis, and its highest point is at (0,1), so it is the upper semicircle with center (0,0) and radius 1. The second segment goes from x=1 to x=3, is located below the x-axis, and its lowest point is at (2,-1), so it is the lower semicircle with center (2,0) and radius 1. Reasoning: The definite integral ∫_{-1}^{3} f(x) dx represents signed area. The upper semicircle contributes positive area (1/2)π(1)^2 = π/2; the lower semicircle contributes negative area -(1/2)π(1)^2 = -π/2. Adding the two parts gives π/2 - π/2 = 0.

method.method_draft: Use an analytic symmetry/formula approach. From the text, split the requested integral at x=1. Evaluate symbolically: ∫_{-1}^{1} sqrt(1-x^2) dx + ∫_{1}^{3} -sqrt(1-(x-2)^2) dx. In the second integral substitute u=x-2, so it becomes -∫_{-1}^{1} sqrt(1-u^2) du, which cancels the first integral. Therefore the value is 0.
